Geometric cues for safe, goal-directed, smooth trajectories.
Geometric supervision is used during training.
We use five energy terms to supervise refinement: footprint clearance, goal progress, retreat penalty, early heading, and path smoothness.

The five names follow the current pipeline figure in figs/pipeline/build_diagram.py. The geometric energy is described in GEAR-Nav Overleaf/main.tex. These editable illustrations explain the terms; they are schematic, not measured robot trajectories. This slide describes the formulation and does not imply every term has a nonzero weight in every run. Geometry supplies supervision during training; it is not an inference input.
Show all five cards together. Historical video timing: 00:20–00:28.
Aggregate path–correction pairs; train on all collected rounds.
Train on the paths the model actually visits.

The current model visits new candidate paths. We query energy-based local corrections at those paths and add the examples to the existing dataset. GEAR learns from all collected rounds, and the updated model generates the next paths. The key is to keep earlier examples while adding supervision where the model now goes.

GEAR-Nav Overleaf/main.tex, Energy-Based Dataset Aggregation. Each example retains the observation, goal, current candidate trajectory, and oracle correction. The first round starts from the structured prior; the diagram depicts the recurring loop after initialization. During training, learned updates use kinematic projection and an energy guard. These details are retained here in notes to keep the slide focused on aggregation. The energy oracle and guard are training-only. All visual paths are conceptual, not measured rollouts. No benchmark or convergence claim is added.

The complex pipeline image was replaced by four native editable cards and one return arrow. Old + New makes retention explicit. The diagram uses the same pale scientific palette and dark slide theme as the adjacent slides.
Earlier paths are retained as the model visits new paths.
Eight real training ESDFs, first four recorded aggregation states per scene.

The current model visits a new path, while paths from earlier rounds remain in the replay dataset. Here, the orange path is the current candidate and the gray dotted paths are earlier retained examples.

Eight separate videos together on one slide. Show only the first four rounds sequentially. No round numbers, Collect / Retain / Train labels, or other text inside the videos. Only ESDF backgrounds, path lines, and their waypoint markers remain. The simultaneous-path request was explicitly retracted.

Recorded source: checkpoints/astar_clearance025_prefix_a6000x4_20260924_eval35000/aggregation_state_00035000.npz, candidate depths 0 through 3 in training condition batch 53. Exact complete-condition fingerprint, source hashes, ESDF arrays, and paths verified. Eight distinct clips were chosen in deterministic slot order, without success filtering. The first ten rounds remain in the local source cache; only the first four are shown. No new model training, inference, or oracle queries were run.

Each scene holds its own ESDF and metric viewport fixed across all states. A common coolwarm range −3 to +3 m is used; negative signed distance is blue, zero white, positive red, and off-grid space dark gray. Canonical +x points right and +y up; metric aspect is preserved. No goal symbols or correction arrows are displayed. Retained gray paths preserve their original coordinates. Animation timing is compressed, and line reveal does not invent intermediate candidate states. These are depth-derived dataset maps and qualitative archived training paths, not a safety or performance result.

GEAR model: learn a correction field

The pretrained visual-language model provides context, while the waypoint expert sees the current trajectory. GEAR predicts a correction and applies a bounded update. This loop is reused at deployment without an ESDF, energy gradient, or energy acceptance test.
